transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

My thoughts jump all over the place and I can’t keep a straight line when I talk or plan anything anymore. It has made it incredibly difficult to manage my daily life and care for my mother since I retired.
Have you been hearing or seeing things that other people don’t, or feeling very suspicious or believing things that others say are not true?

Yes, it's very unsettling... at night I often hear a man and a woman in the next room clearly criticizing how I care for my mother, but no one is ever there. I've also become convinced that the museum board and my neighbors are using clues in the arts newsletter and on the train to plot to push me out, even though my niece shows me emails saying they're just worried about me.
Have you also had a period of feeling unusually high, irritable, or full of energy, with much less need for sleep than usual?

Yes, I've had intense stretches where I feel bizarrely amped up and giddy, though I can suddenly get furious over tiny things. During these times, I race around starting multiple projects at once and will go for days sleeping only two or three hours a night. I don't even feel tired the next day—I just feel this constant buzz of energy.
Have you ever had a similar episode of unusually high energy, little sleep, racing thoughts, or grand ideas before this current one, even if it was less severe?

No, I haven't really experienced anything like this before this past year. Before I retired to care for my mother, my life felt very balanced with my museum work, yoga, and art. These intense, high-energy periods are a completely new and frightening change for me.
Have you ever had a similar episode of unusually high energy, little sleep, racing thoughts, or grand ideas before this current one, even if it was less severe?

No, I really never had anything like this happen before this current period. Before I retired about a year ago, I was always very organized and balanced, and I never experienced these intense, erratic swings or sleepless stretches. It is all completely new and unsettling for me.
How long have these high-energy, little-sleep, racing-thought episodes lasted at a time, and have they been present most of the day nearly every day for at least one week?

Yes, during those stretches, it is absolutely an everyday, all-day feeling where I am buzzing with ideas and barely sleeping. These intense periods usually last for about a week or two at a time before I eventually crash hard. They have been coming and going like this for about six of the past ten months.
During the times when you are not feeling sped up, have you also had periods of feeling very depressed, hopeless, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

Yes, I have long stretches where I feel completely flat and drained, losing all interest in art exhibits, hiking, or talking to my docent friends. I'll just sit in my robe staring at the wall, struggling to find the energy to shower or cook unless my niece basically pushes me to move.

When you hear the voices or feel people are plotting against you, do those experiences happen only when you are feeling very high or very depressed, or do they also continue when your mood feels normal?

They definitely continue even when my mood isn't high or manic. During a long stretch in late summer when my mood felt flat and drained, I was still hearing those voices criticizing me and was convinced there was a plot against me, even though I didn't feel revved up at all.
When you are not feeling depressed or unusually energized, do the voices or beliefs that people are plotting still continue for at least two weeks on their own?

Yes, they do. During a stretch in late summer when my mood felt flat and drained rather than revved up or energized, those experiences continued on their own for several weeks. I still heard those voices commenting on me and remained absolutely convinced that my neighbors and the museum board were coordinating against me.
Have you ever had at least 2 weeks when the voices or suspicious beliefs continued even though you were not depressed, manic, or unusually energized at all?

Yes, that absolutely happened during a long stretch in late summer. My mood just felt flat and drained—not revved up, manic, or energetic at all—yet I still heard those voices commenting on me every day. I also remained completely convinced that my neighbors and the museum board were coordinating against me during those weeks.
During the times when your mood is normal, do the voices or beliefs still continue for at least 2 weeks without any major manic or depressive symptoms?

Yes, that is exactly what happened during late summer when my mood was just flat and drained, without any manic highs or major depressive episodes. Even without those intense mood shifts, the voices criticizing me and my belief that the museum board was plotting against me continued on for several weeks.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when the hallucinations or fixed beliefs were present even though you had no manic or depressive symptoms at all?

Yes, that definitely happened. In late summer, there was a stretch of several weeks where my mood was just flat and drained—not manic or euphoric at all. Yet, during that time, I still heard those voices criticizing me and remained convinced that my neighbors and the museum board were coordinating against me.

Have your mood episodes and the hallucinations/delusions usually happened together, or have there been times when the psychotic symptoms lasted for at least 2 weeks even after the mood symptoms were gone?

Both have actually happened to me. In the spring, when I was highly energetic and barely sleeping, the voices and the feeling of being plotted against were very active at the same time. But in late summer, long after that high mood had faded into a flat, drained feeling, those voices and the belief that people were coordinating against me still persisted on their own for several weeks.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when the voices or fixed beliefs were present even though you had no manic or depressive symptoms at all?

Yes, that did happen during a long stretch in late summer when my mood felt mostly flat and drained rather than revved up, excited, or severely depressed. Yet, during those weeks, I was still hearing those voices commenting on me and remained convinced that my neighbors and the museum board were coordinating against me.
Have there been any times when the voices or beliefs were present for at least 2 weeks while your mood was completely normal, with no depression and no manic symptoms at all?

Yes, during that long stretch in late summer, my mood was just flat and drained, with no manic highs or major depressive episodes at all. Yet, the voices commenting on me and my belief that my neighbors and the museum board were plotting against me continued on for several weeks.

Yes, they definitely lasted on their own during a long stretch in late summer. My mood was completely flat—not high or depressed at all—yet for several weeks I still heard those voices and believed my neighbors and the museum board were coordinating against me.

Yes, during that stretch in late summer, my mood was completely flat and even, with no manic highs or depressive lows at all. It was definitely a period of at least two weeks where those experiences persisted without any mood symptoms.

Yes, those high-energy, amped-up periods definitely last for at least a week, and sometimes up to two weeks before I finally crash.
